units.t: Components of Fitness and Goal Setting

learn: Health-related: cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, body composition.
Skill-related: agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, speed.
A complete fitness plan addresses all health-related components.
check: A complete plan addresses all ___ components.
lessons.try: Assess yourself on each component and identify strengths and weaknesses.

learn: Standardised tests compare your results to healthy fitness zones.
Re-test every 6-8 weeks to measure progress.
Focus on personal improvement.
lessons.try: Complete pre-tests and record them in a fitness log.

learn: SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound.
Intrinsic motivation (enjoyment) lasts longer than extrinsic (rewards).
Track progress and adjust.
lessons.try: Write a 12-week SMART fitness goal with weekly checkpoints.

learn: FITT: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type.
Overload, progression, specificity, reversibility, individuality and recovery.
Increase training load by about 10% per week to avoid injury.
check: Increase training load by about ___ per week.
lessons.try: Design a 4-week progressive plan.

learn: A warm-up raises heart rate and prepares muscles (5-10 minutes, dynamic).
A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate, then static stretching.
Skipping these increases injury risk.
check: Static stretching is best during the...
lessons.try: Lead a dynamic warm-up for the class.

learn: Use proper form, equipment and supervision.
Hydrate and dress for the weather; watch for heat illness.
Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain.
lessons.try: Make a safety checklist for a gym session.

learn: Carbohydrates fuel exercise; proteins repair muscle; fats provide long-term energy.
Iron and calcium are especially important for teens.
Eat a variety of whole foods.
lessons.try: Plan meals for a training day.

learn: Drink water throughout the day and during exercise.
Thirst, dark urine and fatigue signal dehydration.
Sports drinks are for long, intense exercise; energy drinks are not recommended for teens.
lessons.try: Track your water intake for three days.

learn: Read labels; limit added sugar, sodium and saturated fat.
Fast food can fit occasionally with balanced choices.
Avoid fad diets; consult a doctor or dietitian.
check: Expert nutrition advice comes from a...
lessons.try: Analyse a fast-food menu for healthier options.

learn: Teens need 8-10 hours; sleep cycles include light, deep and REM sleep.
Deep sleep repairs the body; REM sleep supports memory and learning.
Sleep deprivation harms mood, grades, reaction time and immunity.
lessons.try: Keep a sleep diary and analyse patterns.

learn: Stress triggers the fight-or-flight response: adrenaline, faster heart rate, tense muscles.
Eustress (positive) can motivate; distress (negative) harms health.
Chronic stress affects sleep, immunity and mental health.
lessons.try: Identify your top three stressors.

learn: Healthy coping: exercise, breathing, mindfulness, time management, talking, hobbies.
Unhealthy coping: substance use, avoidance, overeating, isolation.
Build a personal stress management plan.
lessons.try: Practise a five-minute mindfulness exercise.

learn: Common conditions include anxiety disorders, depression, eating disorders and ADHD.
Mental illness is common and treatable; it is not a weakness.
Stigma prevents people from seeking help.
lessons.try: Research one condition and its treatments.

learn: Warning signs: withdrawal, changes in sleep or appetite, hopelessness, talking about death.
Take all talk of suicide seriously.
Tell a trusted adult immediately; call or text 988 in the US.
check: Withdrawal from friends can be a...
lessons.try: Make a support card with trusted adults and helplines.

learn: Resilience grows from relationships, coping skills and purpose.
Gratitude, exercise and sleep support wellbeing.
Helping others improves your own mental health.
lessons.try: Keep a gratitude journal for a week.

learn: Nicotine is highly addictive and harms the developing brain.
Vaping can cause lung injury; flavours attract young users.
Quitting is hard but possible with support.
lessons.try: Analyse vaping marketing strategies.

learn: Alcohol affects judgment and coordination; drinking and driving kills.
Cannabis affects memory, attention and motivation in teens.
Mixing substances multiplies risks.
lessons.try: Discuss scenarios involving peer pressure at a party.

learn: Opioids are highly addictive; misuse can cause fatal overdose.
Counterfeit pills may contain fentanyl, which can be deadly in tiny amounts.
Never take pills that weren't prescribed to you.
lessons.try: Learn the signs of an overdose and how to get emergency help.

learn: Healthy: respect, trust, honesty, communication, equality, independence.
Unhealthy: jealousy, control, manipulation, put-downs.
Abusive: physical, emotional, sexual or digital harm.
check: Checking a partner's phone constantly is...
lessons.try: Evaluate relationship scenarios as healthy, unhealthy or abusive.

learn: Consent is clear, enthusiastic, ongoing and freely given.
It can be withdrawn at any time; silence or intoxication is not consent.
Respect boundaries in every relationship.
lessons.try: Discuss consent scenarios in small groups.

learn: Talk to a trusted adult, counsellor or hotline about unhealthy relationships.
Support friends without judgment.
Digital safety: don't share passwords or private images.
check: Sharing private images can lead to...
lessons.try: List resources for relationship help.

learn: Pathogens: bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.
Vaccines train the immune system; hand washing prevents spread.
Antibiotic resistance grows when antibiotics are misused.
lessons.try: Explain how vaccines create immunity.

learn: Heart disease, cancer, stroke and diabetes are leading causes of death.
Risk factors: tobacco, inactivity, poor diet, excess alcohol.
Screening and healthy habits reduce risk.
check: A leading cause of death is...
lessons.try: Make a plan to reduce your future chronic disease risk.

learn: Regular check-ups, dental care, sun protection and hearing protection.
Know family health history.
Advocate for your own health with doctors.
lessons.try: Prepare questions for a doctor's visit.

learn: Basketball, soccer, volleyball, ultimate frisbee and softball build fitness and teamwork.
Strategy: spacing, communication, transition.
Sportsmanship and leadership matter as much as skill.
lessons.try: Play a team sport and reflect on your role.

learn: Tennis, badminton, golf, track, swimming and climbing can be played for life.
Technique, practice and self-motivation drive progress.
Many have clubs and community leagues.
lessons.try: Try a new individual sport and set a skill goal.

learn: Adults need 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly plus strength training twice a week.
Find activities you enjoy and fit them into daily life.
Active living reduces disease and improves mood.
check: Strength training is recommended ___ times a week.
lessons.try: Write a personal lifetime activity plan.

learn: Check-Call-Care: check the scene and victim, call 911, give care.
Use gloves; Good Samaritan laws protect helpers.
Don't move someone with a suspected head, neck or back injury.
check: The first step is to check the...
Don't move someone with a suspected ___ injury.
lessons.try: Practise an emergency call script.

learn: Bleeding: direct pressure. Burns: cool water. Sprains: RICE.
Shock: keep the person lying down and warm.
Allergic reactions: use an epinephrine auto-injector if prescribed and call 911.
lessons.try: Practise bandaging and the recovery position.

learn: Hands-only CPR: push hard and fast, 100-120 per minute, 2 inches deep.
AEDs analyse rhythm and talk you through steps.
Certification courses teach full CPR.
check: CPR compressions are about ___ deep for adults.
lessons.try: Find a CPR certification course near you.
